title: CI tails come from unsharded suites and per-job fixed costs — shard first, cache transforms, then share the build
summary: test(scripts) was an 11min unsharded tail; vitest --shard needs only matrix wiring. fsModuleCache persists content-hashed transforms and restores via actions/cache. Per-shard install+build (~4min) is the next fixed cost — a shared build-artifact job or duration-aware split needs timing data first.
procedure_steps: (1) Find the tail by job durations, not job count — one unsharded suite dominated the whole pipeline. (2) vitest --shard=N/M is a pure-CI change when the dispatcher forwards args; pin the passthrough in a unit test. (3) fsModuleCache caches transforms keyed by content hash — safe to restore across runs via actions/cache with a config-hash key and prefix restore-keys. (4) vitest `list` ignores --shard — verify splits on `run`. (5) Beyond a point, more shards lose to fixed per-job setup (install+build ~4min each); the next lever is a shared build artifact, not more shards.
safety_notes: Require approval before irreversible or high-risk actions.
Capture evidence before and after the action.
escalation_conditions: Result does not match the expected state
